job.title: IT Manager
job.description:
About the company

Our client is an established, family-owned Sydney construction company delivering projects across Sydney, the Southern Highlands and the Central Coast. Around 65 people work across the business: a small office team and a larger group on project sites.
The owners are hands-on and accessible, and the culture is practical, supportive and loyal. Average staff tenure sits above four years, and many people have been with the business for much longer. Like the rest of the industry, the company relies more on technology every year, from project management and document control to estimating, procurement, safety and finance platforms.

About the role

This is the business's first in-house IT role. Until now, IT has been handled by a managed service provider, with day-to-day coordination falling to people whose real jobs sit elsewhere. The business wants someone on the ground who knows its people, its systems and its sites, and who can resolve issues quickly.
You will be the IT function. There is no team to manage: you will look after users in the office and on site, keep devices, systems and security in good order, and work directly with the directors. In the first few months you will also lead the handover from the current provider, which will involve some overlap and untangling as responsibilities move in-house.
Alongside the day-to-day, there is room to improve how things work. The business uses a range of cloud platforms, and some information is still moved between them by hand. You will have scope to spot those inefficiencies and remove them using automation and the AI tools the business already licenses.

Key responsibilities

User support

  • Provide first-line and escalation support to around 65 users, from tech-savvy office staff to site managers and foremen, by phone, in person and on site.
  • Resolve access, connectivity and hardware issues quickly, including SharePoint and mapped drive connections, email and printing.
  • Deliver practical training so people get more out of the tools they use every day.

Systems and access

  • Manage the Microsoft 365 environment, including SharePoint, Entra ID and Intune.
  • Run onboarding and offboarding: accounts, devices, permissions and licences.
  • Support users across the business's cloud platforms, including project management, document control, estimating, procurement, safety, finance and design tools, working with each vendor where needed.

Devices and assets

  • Own the device lifecycle for laptops, mobiles and iPads: purchasing, setup, rebuilds, warranty claims and retirement.
  • Maintain the asset register and manage software licences.
  • Manage printers and photocopiers across leased and owned equipment.
  • Look after the mobile fleet through the business telco account, including mobile security settings such as geofencing and overseas roaming.

Project sites

  • Set up and decommission site offices, including routers, Starlink, hubs, printers and connectivity.
    Visit sites as needed, typically every month or two, to set up, support or bring equipment back.

Security and risk

  • Keep security settings and practices current across devices, accounts and systems.
    Respond to cyber insurance questionnaires and checks, and close off any gaps they identify.

Vendors and improvement

  • Manage relationships with hardware suppliers, software vendors, the telco provider and the outgoing managed service provider.
  • Identify manual processes, such as re-keying data between systems, and automate them where it makes sense, including with the business's AI tools.

Skills and experience

Essential

  • Solid hands-on experience as a senior IT generalist, systems administrator or IT support lead, ideally as the sole or lead IT person in an SMB or mid-market business.
  • A tertiary qualification in IT or a related field.
  • Strong working knowledge of Microsoft 365, SharePoint, Entra ID and Intune or similar MDM tools.
  • Proven ability to run IT autonomously and manage competing priorities without day-to-day technical guidance.
  • A stable career history.
  • Clear, patient communication with non-technical users, and the confidence to support busy, direct site teams.
  • Australian citizenship and eligibility to obtain a security clearance.
  • Happy to work from the office five days a week and travel to project sites.

Highly regarded

  • Exposure to security best practice and governance, including cyber insurance requirements.
  • Experience with process automation or practical use of AI tools.
  • Experience with construction platforms such as Procore, or a background in construction or another project-based industry.
  • Experience with site networks, Starlink and mobile fleet management.

Who will thrive here

  • The people who succeed in this business are practical and earn trust by helping. The best fit is someone who enjoys the technical work but would rather be out solving problems with people than sitting behind a screen all day.
  • Service-minded. You pick up the phone, follow through, and understand that a site manager with a broken laptop needs an answer now.
  • Thick-skinned and patient. Construction sites move fast and people are direct. You stay calm and keep things moving.
  • Curious. You keep up with where technology is heading, including security and AI, and you look for better ways of doing things.
  • Self-directed. You are comfortable owning a function end to end, setting your own priorities and explaining technical decisions in plain English to non-technical owners.

Why join

  • A role you can shape. It is brand new, so you build the IT function your way rather than inheriting someone else's setup.
  • Stability. A steady, non-tech business with long staff tenure, away from the restructures and redundancies across much of the tech sector.
  • Visible impact. You will work directly with hands-on owners, replacing a service the business has outgrown, so good work is noticed quickly.
  • Real variety. User support, site work, security and automation, all in one role.

How to apply

If you are a hands-on IT all-rounder ready to own the function and make a visible difference, we would love to hear from you. For a confidential conversation, contact Craig Nel at Cox Purtell [ ]

job.title: Executive Assistant
job.description:
Executive Assistant to the General Manager
Mascot, Sydney (moving to the CBD)
Salary: $90 – $110k + Super (dependent on experience)
12-month maternity leave contract
Hybrid – WFH and WFO

About the client
Our client is a global medical aesthetics company with a well-established ANZ business based in Sydney. The local team works closely with regional and global colleagues across APAC, giving the role genuine international exposure. It's a collaborative office where leaders are approachable and people are trusted to get on with the job.

About the role
Reporting to the General Manager, you'll provide executive support while taking ownership of workplace operations and key business projects. The headline project is the planned office relocation, which you'll coordinate through fit-out and the physical move. This is a 12-month maternity leave contract running until mid-January 2028. The role suits a self-starter who enjoys variety and real ownership.

Duties

  • Manage the General Manager's domestic and APAC travel, expenses, diary changes and meeting coordination.
  • Coordinate the office relocation, working with project managers, the leadership team and suppliers on layout, fit-out and the move itself.
  • Act as the first point of contact for office and facilities matters, managing vendors, contractors, supplies, ordering and invoice reconciliation.
  • Coordinate up to three sales conferences a year, including a larger offsite conference with an awards dinner, in partnership with the events team.
  • Support the General Manager with reporting, presentations and company communications, and drive other business projects such as systems improvements.

Requirements

  • Solid experience as an Executive Assistant supporting a senior leader at director level or above.
  • Demonstrated experience leading or coordinating business projects with minimal direction. Office relocation or fit-out experience will be highly regarded.
  • Experience managing domestic and international travel and expenses. Concur knowledge is a plus.
  • Office or facilities management experience, including working with suppliers and managing purchasing.
  • Event coordination experience, ideally including conferences or offsite events.
  • Advanced Microsoft 365 skills, including PowerPoint, Excel and Teams.
  • Availability to start in December, with flexibility for extra office days around events and business needs.

How to apply
If this sounds like the right next step for you, we'd love to hear from you, so please apply now.

job.title: Office Manager
job.description:
Office Manager
6-Month Contract - potential to extend
Sydney CBD
$100,000 + super FTE

About the client

Our client is a global technology organisation with a growing presence across Australia and New Zealand. Their regional offices sit within a well-established international workplace and facilities function, with strong support from regional and global leadership. They place real value on creating offices that are welcoming, inclusive and run smoothly, so their people can focus on doing great work.

About the role

Based in their Sydney CBD office, you will be the go-to person for office operations and facilities, while also supporting the Melbourne office too. This is a hands-on, on-site role where you will look after everything from front desk responsibilities, vendors and building management to physical security, safety compliance and the local budget. You will be the face of the office for staff and visitors in this 6-month engagement, which starts quickly and may extend to 12 months.

Duties

  • Oversee day-to-day office operations across Sydney with some support for the Melbourne office (there are 2 small offices in Perth and Auckland too), including front desk, mailroom, supplies, amenities and general upkeep.
  • Manage relationships with landlords, building management and facility vendors such as cleaning, security and catering, including tracking SLAs and KPIs.
  • Act as the local physical security point of contact, managing access control, badge and visitor management, incident response and emergency drills.
  • Manage the local operating budget, raising purchase orders, matching vendor invoices and flagging variances against forecast.
  • Partner with HR, Talent Acquisition and local leadership to prepare for new starters and coordinate office events, celebrations and culture initiatives.

Requirements

  • 5+ years of experience in office coordination, workplace services or facilities management, ideally within a multinational technology or corporate environment.
  • Proven experience managing vendors and contractors, including reviewing quotes, negotiating contracts and tracking service performance.
  • Sound knowledge of building management practices and Australian workplace health and safety, fire safety and security requirements.
  • Experience managing an operating budget, purchase orders and invoice reconciliation.
  • Confidence using workplace technology such as Google Workspace, Slack, Zoom and ticketing systems like ServiceNow.
  • Comfortable overseeing multiple sites and handling executive escalations calmly and professionally.
  • Available to work on-site 5 days a week in the Sydney CBD for a 6-month contract.

Further information about this role

While this is a temporary contract, it comes with the benefits of a permanent role. You’ll be paid a monthly salary and accrue pro-rata annual leave, along with paid sick leave and NSW public holidays.

If this sounds like the right next step for you, we would love to hear from you, so please apply today.

job.title: Linux Systems Engineer (Bare Metal & Kubernetes)
job.description:
About the Role

As Linux Systems Engineer, you'll join the Global Linux team responsible for the infrastructure that powers a live trading environment, spanning large-scale bare-metal Linux platforms and on-prem Kubernetes clusters. You'll design, build and operate systems the business depends on every day, from hardware provisioning through to orchestration and automation. This is ownership of foundational infrastructure, not managed cloud abstraction, in a setting where reliability and performance matter.

Duties

  • Design, deploy and operate on-prem Kubernetes clusters in a bare-metal environment.
  • Maintain and improve bare-metal Linux infrastructure, including provisioning, lifecycle management and performance tuning.
  • Own and operate core Kubernetes components such as the CNI, GitOps tooling and cluster management layer (currently Cilium, ArgoCD and Rancher).
  • Build and maintain CI/CD workflows and infrastructure as code for infrastructure and cluster deployments.
  • Take part in an on-call rotation, drive post-incident improvements, and document runbooks so the wider team can support the platforms.

Requirements

  • Strong Linux systems engineering experience in a production environment.
  • Hands-on experience running Kubernetes or comparable infrastructure on-prem, not solely through managed cloud offerings.
  • Experience with infrastructure as code and CI/CD or GitOps workflows. Terraform, ArgoCD, Rancher, Cilium and GitHub Actions are all useful, and depth in the specific stack can be built on the job.
  • Solid understanding of networking fundamentals, including L2/L3, routing, firewalls and load balancing.
  • Experience troubleshooting performance issues across the kernel, container and network layers.
  • A production mindset, with experience in incident response and post-mortem-driven improvement.
  • Experience with Prometheus, Grafana, Kubernetes security controls, or low-latency and high-performance environments will be highly regarded.

If this sounds like the kind of infrastructure challenge you're after, we'd love to hear from you.

job.title: Operations & Membership Officer
job.description:
Operations & Membership Officer

Chirnside Park, VIC

Full time

Interstate and occasional international travel a few times a year



Whether your background is in events, marketing, account management or B2B partnerships, this role is a chance to take your skills into a national peak industry body. You'll coordinate trade shows (with international travel), drive member growth, manage sponsor relationships and deliver marketing campaigns, with a lot of variety from one week to the next. No association experience is needed, just the energy to get stuck in.

The organisation runs industry-leading events, including a flagship triennial trade exhibition, alongside a strong member services and partnerships program. With over 150 Australian-based company members, this is a genuinely varied role working closely with the General Manager, CEO and business partners across the full operations of the association.



What you'll be doing:

  • Delivering clear, timely reporting on acquisition, sponsorship revenue, event performance and marketing engagement.
  • Proactively identifying, targeting and converting new member companies to drive satisfaction, retention and growth.
  • Coordinating the association's presence at domestic and international trade events, from stand design and staffing through to marketing and lead follow-up.
  • Building and nurturing relationships with sponsors and service partners, and pitching new partners that resonate with the membership.
  • Driving member communications across newsletters, LinkedIn, forums and other digital channels, including publications and member content.
  • Managing the association's recurring events calendar, including its flagship exhibition, an annual awards program, and other member gatherings.


What we're looking for:

  • 5+ years' experience in a customer-facing, coordination or business operations role (association, events or B2B environment preferred).
  • Marketing experience (mainly social media and EDM creation).
  • Strong relationship management and communication skills.
  • Ability to work autonomously and manage multiple projects simultaneously.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills in a professional context.


Great to have (not essential):

  • Background in events coordination or trade exhibition delivery.
  • Exposure to sponsorship or partnership management.
  • Familiarity with the packaging, processing or broader manufacturing sector.


This is a fantastic opportunity for a relationship-driven operator who wants genuine variety, autonomy and the chance to play a key role in the continued success of a peak industry body.



Salary is competitive and commensurate with experience, circa $90,000 to $100,000 plus superannuation, with interstate and occasional international travel a few times a year.

job.title: Customer Success Program Manager (Fortune 500 SaaS)
job.description:
Customer Success Program Manager

$126.6k + Super | 9 month contract | Flexible Hybrid Role | Sydney CBD Based

About the client

Our client is a global Fortune 500 SaaS company whose software platforms is a leader in the Fintech space. With an established presence in Australia, the business works closely with international teams to deliver for its local customers. It values practical problem solving, clear communication and continuous improvement in how work gets done.

About the role

This is a 9-month contract, hands-on individual contributor role delivering Customer Success programs on the ground in Australia. You will take agreed priorities and turn them into practical plans, coordinate the people involved and keep work moving through to completion. Reporting into a UK-based team while working closely with Australian stakeholders, you will be the local driver of delivery. It suits someone who enjoys organising work, solving problems and improving how a business operates.

Duties

  • Plan and deliver local Customer Success projects and program activities from start to finish.
  • Build clear project plans with tasks, owners, deadlines and key milestones.
  • Work with Australian and UK teams to agree priorities and follow up on actions.
  • Track progress, identify delays or risks early and help resolve issues before they escalate.
  • Prepare updates and business reports, and use feedback and data to recommend practical improvements.

Requirements

  • Around 3 to 5 years of experience in project management, program delivery or business operations.
  • Industry experience within large SaaS or Fintech is highly desirable
  • A proven track record of taking projects from planning through to completion.
  • Strong organisation skills and the ability to manage several priorities at once.
  • Confidence working across different teams and adapting when requirements are unclear or priorities change.
  • Working ability with spreadsheets and presentations for reporting and updates.
  • Basic familiarity with AI tools and a willingness to learn how to use approved tools responsibly.
  • Flexibility to attend agreed meetings across Australian and UK time zones.
  • Experience in Customer Success, customer operations or a software or technology business is advantageous, but not essential.

How to apply

If this sounds like the next step for you, we would love to hear from you, hit APPLY NOW for immediate consideration.
